turns.question: Where is the structural map engine implemented, and how is the parser engine selected per file?
turns.text:
This confirms the exact selection logic. Now let's check `treeSitterEntry`/`languageConfigs` in treesitter.go and `rulesForPath` in regex.go for completeness, plus how `--map` CLI flag wires into this (the `--map-engine` flag mentioned in README).Now let's find where `internal/ghx` calls `mapengine.Map` to complete the wiring picture.I have everything needed to answer confidently.

## Structural map engine implementation

**Location:** `internal/mapengine/` (Go package `mapengine`), 5 files:

- **`types.go`** — engine-agnostic types (`Engine`, `Level`, `Kind`, `Options`, `Result`, `Symbol`) and the top-level dispatcher `Map(path, content, opts)` (`types.go:125`), plus the auto-selection logic `mapAuto` (`types.go:143`) and fallback wrapper `mapTreeSitterWithFallback` (`types.go:160`). Also does symbol sorting/dedup/formatting via `buildResultFromSymbols` (`types.go:174`).
- **`goast.go`** — `GoASTMapper` (`goast.go:11,13`), uses Go's standard `go/ast` + `go/token` to walk top-level declarations (`goASTSymbols`, `goGenDeclSymbols`, `goFuncDeclSymbol`), preserving full multi-line signatures and generics.
- **`treesitter.go`** — `TreeSitterMapper` (`treesitter.go:12,25`), built on the `gotreesitter` library (`github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter`) with a `grammars` package for language detection (`grammars.DetectLanguage`, `treesitter.go:89`). Per-language configs live in `defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs()` (`treesitter.go:281`) for go, typescript, tsx, javascript, python, rust — each with its own tag query, signature formatter, and merge-with-regex behavior (e.g. Rust `use` imports aren't tagged by the tree-sitter grammar, so they're merged in from regex).
- **`regex.go`** — `RegexMapper` (`regex.go:10,82`), line-by-line regex rules keyed by file extension in the `regexRules` map (`regex.go:20`) covering go, ts/tsx/js/jsx, py, rs, java, kt, rb, with a generic fallback rule set in `rulesForPath` (`regex.go:105`) for unlisted extensions.

## Per-file engine selection

Selection happens in `mapengine.Map` (`internal/mapengine/types.go:125`), which normalizes the requested engine (`normalizeEngine`, `types.go:80` — only `regex`/`tree-sitter` are recognized explicitly; anything else, including empty/default, becomes `auto`) then switches:

- **explicit `regex`** → `RegexMapper{}.Map(...)` directly.
- **explicit `tree-sitter`** → `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., warnUnsupported=true)`, i.e. tree-sitter with a regex fallback on error (and a warning surfaced if it fails, unless it's simply an unsupported language, though `warnUnsupported=true` here means it always warns).
- **`auto`** (the default) → `mapAuto` (`types.go:143`), which branches on the file extension via `filepath.Ext`:
  - `.go` → `GoASTMapper`; on error, falls back to `RegexMapper` (marking `Fallback: true`).
  - `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.py`, `.rs` → `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., warnUnsupported=false)` (tree-sitter, silently falling back to regex if the language isn't actually supported by the tagger).
  - everything else → `RegexMapper` directly.
- **unknown engine string** in the non-normalized path (defensive `default` case in the outer `switch`) → regex with a `"unknown mapper engine"` warning — effectively dead code today since `normalizeEngine` already coerces anything unrecognized to `auto`.

This matches the README's description exactly ("Go uses go/ast... TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Rust use gotreesitter... everything else falls back to regex").

## Wiring from the CLI/MCP surface

- CLI: `internal/cli/ghx.go` reads flags `--level`, `--kind`, `--map-engine` (default `"auto"`, line 211) and passes them into `ghxlib.ReadOpts{MapEngine: ...}` (lines 110–121).
- MCP server: `internal/cli/serve.go` exposes the same as a `mapEngine` tool parameter (lines 90–92, 220–230).
- Both funnel into `internal/ghx/read.go:187-190`, which calls `mapengine.Map(path, []byte(text), mapengine.Options{Engine: mapengine.Engine(opts.MapEngine), ...})` — the actual engine-selection entry point described above.

**Not verified:** I did not read the full bodies of `goast.go`'s symbol-extraction helpers, the complete `treesitter.go` tagger/query-building code, or the `grammars` package (`grammars.DetectLanguage`/`LangEntry`) itself — only their signatures via `--map` and the specific lines relevant to selection logic. I also didn't execute the binary; conclusions are from static reading of source via `ghx read`.

README:
# ghx — GitHub Code Exploration for AI Agents

One command does what takes 3-5 API calls. Batch file reads, code maps, search — all via `gh` CLI. Write JS programs that compose operations in one round-trip.

## Why

An agent wants to understand `packages/shadcn/src/utils/` in [shadcn-ui/ui](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui):

**With `gh` CLI** — 4 turns, 4 API calls, reads 3 full files (3,761 tokens), sees 3 of 34 files:
```
gh api /repos/shadcn-ui/ui/contents/packages/shadcn/src/utils       → JSON with shas, urls, links (480 tokens for a file list)
gh api /repos/.../get-config.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (1,981 tokens — agent only needed exports)
gh api /repos/.../registries.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (676 tokens)
gh api /repos/.../frameworks.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (624 tokens)
```

**With ghx** — 2 turns, 2 API calls, maps 10 files (3,058 tokens), sees signatures of all 10:
```
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui packages/shadcn/src/utils                     → directory listing (199 tokens)
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui "packages/shadcn/src/utils/*.ts" --map        → signatures of 10 files (2,859 tokens)
```

Same token budget. The `gh` agent read 3 full files. The ghx agent saw the structure of 10 — imports, exports, function signatures — and knows which ones to drill into. Pass a file, get content. Pass a directory, get a listing. Pass a glob, get matching files. Same command, always useful output.
